newsitem.title: MALTA: Bond market overshadows equities in Malta trading.
newsitem.headline: Bond market overshadows equities in Malta trading.

text.p: Two large block trades saw business in government bonds dominate trading at the Malta stock exchange on Wednesday.
Market turnover in the once-weekly trading session reached Lm1.19 million ($3.3 million) of which Lm1.13 million was in government bonds.
Trading in equities was down, with the share index dropping by 5.18 to 1008.18 points as all share prices slumped.
Business in equities amounted to just over Lm39,100 with 28,346 shares changing hands in 44 deals.
Of these 13,050 were Bank of Valletta shares transacted in 23 deals for an average 124 cents each, down one cent.
There were 15 deals in Mid-Med Bank, with 13,000 shares selling for an average 149 cents, also down one cent.
Lombard Bank Malta shares were down an average seven mils, with 2,296 shares changing hands for an average 153.3 cents.
Farsons ordinary shares lost one cent, with 3,000 shares selling for an average 51 cents.
There were 64 deals in fixed income securities. Business in government bonds was mainly in the six percent MGS 1999 and the six percent MGS 1998(V) in which two large block trades were made.
There were 17 deals in Mid-Med Bank 7.25 percent unsecured loan stock 2005 amounting to a market value of Lm18,254.
